description: Red flag symptoms requiring immediate medical attention and guidance on when to seek care

entries.title: CRITICAL: Post-Menopausal Bleeding
entries.description: Any bleeding after 12 months without periods - URGENT
entries.content: Post-menopausal bleeding is ANY spotting or bleeding after you have gone 12 consecutive months without a period. This is NEVER normal and requires urgent medical evaluation to rule out uterine or cervical cancer. While it's often due to benign causes like thinning tissues, it must always be investigated.
entries.why_its_serious: Can be early sign of uterine or cervical cancer; early detection is crucial
what_doctor_will_do: Transvaginal ultrasound to measure uterine lining thickness
entries.chatbot_response: ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Post-menopausal bleeding requires urgent medical evaluation. Please contact your doctor within 24-48 hours or visit urgent care. While often benign, this must be checked to rule out serious conditions.

entries.title: CRITICAL: Cognitive Changes Beyond Brain Fog
entries.description: Forgetting how to perform familiar tasks
entries.content: Brain fog (forgetting names, losing keys) is normal in menopause. However, forgetting HOW to do familiar tasks (like driving to a familiar place, using the stove, or performing work tasks you've done for years) is NOT normal brain fog and requires neurological evaluation.
entries.distinction: Brain fog = forgetting WHAT (names, words). Concerning = forgetting HOW (to do familiar tasks)
entries.why_its_serious: May indicate neurological issues requiring early intervention, not just hormonal brain fog
what_doctor_will_do: Rule out other causes (thyroid, B12 deficiency, depression)
entries.chatbot_response: This sounds more serious than typical menopause brain fog. Please see your doctor within the week for a cognitive assessment. Forgetting how to do familiar tasks needs medical evaluation.

entries.title: URGENT: New Heart Palpitations
entries.description: New irregular heartbeat or racing heart
entries.content: While heart palpitations can be caused by estrogen loss affecting heart rhythm, NEW palpitations must be checked via ECG to rule out actual heart conditions (arrhythmias) which increase after menopause. Especially urgent if accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness.
entries.urgency: URGENT if with chest pain/SOB - ER. Otherwise see doctor within 1 week
when_to_go_to_er: Palpitations lasting more than a few minutes
entries.why_its_serious: Could be hormonal OR could be cardiac arrhythmia requiring treatment
entries.chatbot_response: ⚠️ New heart palpitations need medical evaluation. If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness with palpitations, go to ER immediately. Otherwise, see your doctor within a week for an ECG.

entries.title: HIGH PRIORITY: Heavy Bleeding or Flooding
entries.description: Soaking through pad/tampon every hour or passing large clots
entries.content: While irregular heavy periods can occur in perimenopause, flooding (soaking through protection every hour for several hours) or passing clots larger than a quarter requires medical evaluation. This can lead to anemia and may indicate fibroids, polyps, or other conditions requiring treatment.
entries.urgency: See doctor within 1-2 weeks; sooner if causing anemia symptoms (dizziness, extreme fatigue)
warning_signs: Soaking through pad/tampon every hour for 2+ hours
Passing clots larger than a quarter
Symptoms of anemia (extreme fatigue, dizziness, pale skin, shortness of breath)
entries.why_its_serious: Can cause anemia; may indicate treatable conditions like fibroids or polyps
what_doctor_will_do: Blood count to check for anemia

entries.title: HIGH PRIORITY: Severe Breast Pain or New Lumps
entries.description: Localized breast pain or palpable lumps
entries.content: While breast tenderness is common in perimenopause due to hormonal fluctuations, severe localized pain or any new lump requires evaluation. Most lumps are benign, but breast cancer risk increases with age.
what_doctor_will_do: Referral to breast specialist if needed

entries.title: Symptoms Severely Affecting Quality of Life
entries.description: When symptoms interfere with daily functioning
entries.content: You don't have to suffer through menopause. If symptoms are significantly affecting your work, relationships, sleep, or mental health, you deserve treatment. Effective options are available.
when_symptoms_warrant_treatment: Unable to sleep more than a few hours per night
Anxiety or depression interfering with daily life
Hot flashes disrupting daily activities multiple times per day
entries.important_message: Menopause is natural, but suffering is not mandatory. Treatment can dramatically improve quality of life.
what_to_prepare: List of all current medications and supplements

entries.title: Preparing for Your Menopause Appointment
entries.description: How to get the most from your doctor visit
entries.content: Preparation is key to getting appropriate care for menopause symptoms. Many doctors have limited menopause training, so being informed and organized helps ensure you get the care you need.
entries.symptom_tracking: Keep a symptom tracker for 2-4 weeks before visit noting: which symptoms, severity (1-10), frequency, triggers, impact on daily life
information_to_bring: Complete list of symptoms with severity ratings
Menstrual pattern (dates of last several periods)
Family history (especially breast cancer, heart disease, osteoporosis)
questions_to_ask: Is my symptom profile consistent with my age/stage of menopause?
What are the risks vs. benefits of HRT for my specific situation and family history?
What are all my treatment options (hormonal and non-hormonal)?
How do we monitor for side effects?
Are there any tests I need (bone density, cardiovascular screening)?
entries.finding_specialist: Look for 'MSC' (Menopause Society Certified) practitioners or gynecologists with menopause focus
if_doctor_dismissive: Ask directly: 'What are my options for managing these symptoms?'
Bring printed symptom tracker showing impact
Consider finding a new provider if consistently dismissed

entries.title: Finding a Menopause Specialist
entries.description: How to find knowledgeable menopause care providers
entries.content: Not all healthcare providers have extensive menopause training. Finding a specialist or certified practitioner can make a significant difference in the quality of care you receive.
certifications_to_look_for: NCMP (North American Menopause Society Certified Menopause Practitioner)
where_to_search: Academic medical centers with menopause clinics
what_to_ask_when_calling: Do you have providers certified in menopause care?
What percentage of your practice focuses on menopause?
Do you prescribe HRT? What types?
What is your approach to menopause management?
red_flags: Refuses to discuss HRT without medical contraindication
Doesn't ask about symptom impact on quality of life
Pushes unregulated supplements instead of evidence-based treatment

entries.title: Regular Health Screenings After Menopause
entries.description: Preventive care and monitoring in postmenopause
entries.content: Postmenopause requires specific health screenings due to increased risks for certain conditions. Regular monitoring helps catch problems early when they're most treatable.

recommended_screenings.frequency: Baseline at menopause or age 65; repeat based on results
recommended_screenings.why: Screen for osteoporosis; guides treatment decisions

recommended_screenings.frequency: Annually or every 2 years (discuss with doctor)
Per guidelines (often can stop at 65 if previous normal results)
Blood pressure annually; cholesterol every 3-5 years or as recommended
recommended_screenings.why: Heart disease risk increases after menopause

recommended_screenings.frequency: Every 3 years or more often if risk factors
Starting at 45-50, then every 10 years if normal

annual_checkup_should_include: Discussion of symptoms and quality of life

entries.title: When Symptoms Return or Worsen
entries.content: If you're on treatment and symptoms return or worsen, or if new symptoms develop, follow-up with your healthcare provider is needed. Treatment may need adjustment.
situations_requiring_follow_up: Symptoms return while on HRT (may need dose adjustment)
entries.dont_wait: Don't suffer in silence or assume treatment isn't working. Many issues can be resolved with dose or formulation adjustments.
